title: Unsweetened cocoa powder: fiber, fat, protein, and minerals

seo.title: Unsweetened cocoa: fiber, fat, protein and minerals
seo.meta_description: See how much fiber, fat, protein, magnesium and iron unsweetened cocoa powder contains—and why a tablespoon tells a different story from 100 grams.
seo.search_intent: Understand the nutritional composition of unsweetened cocoa powder

excerpt: Unsweetened cocoa powder is highly concentrated: the USDA reference provides about 37 g fiber, 19.6 g protein, and 13.7 g fat per 100 g, plus substantial magnesium, iron, and copper. A tablespoon is only about 5–6 g, so real serving amounts are much smaller.
content_html:
Cocoa powder looks spectacular on a per-100-gram nutrition table: lots of fiber, meaningful protein, and very high mineral numbers. But 100 g of cocoa powder is far more than a normal serving. A tablespoon is only about 5–6 g, so both views are needed.

What unsweetened cocoa provides per 100 g

The USDA Standard Reference entry for unsweetened cocoa powder lists about 228 calories, 37 g fiber, 19.6 g protein, and 13.7 g fat per 100 g, with only about 1.8 g total sugars.

NutrientPer 100 gPer 5.4 g (about 1 tbsp)
Calories228~12
Protein19.6 g~1.1 g
Fat13.7 g~0.7 g
Fiber37 g~2.0 g

The gap matters. Cocoa is nutrient-dense by weight, yet the spoonful added to oatmeal or yogurt contributes modest absolute amounts. Two tablespoons can add several grams of fiber, but they do not turn the meal into a high-protein food.

Why the fiber number is so high

Cocoa powder is made from cocoa solids after some cocoa butter has been pressed out. Removing part of the fat concentrates the nonfat portion of the bean, including cell-wall material and fiber.

That is why powder can contain far more fiber by weight than finished chocolate. The USDA reference for 70–85% dark chocolate contains about 10.9 g fiber/100 g, compared with 37 g in the unsweetened cocoa entry.

Cocoa powder still contains fat

Powdered cocoa does not mean fat-free cocoa. The amount left after pressing varies by product. European rules, for example, distinguish standard cocoa powder from fat-reduced cocoa using the proportion of cocoa butter in dry matter.

Cocoa fat is dominated by stearic, palmitic, and oleic acids. A spoonful contributes little total fat, but a baking recipe using a large amount of cocoa can make the difference more noticeable.

Is cocoa powder a protein food?

At 19.6 g protein per 100 g, the concentration looks impressive. At one tablespoon, it is only around 1 g. Cocoa can contribute to a meal's protein total, but it is not usually the main protein source.

Minerals are the other standout

Per 100 g, the USDA entry provides roughly 499 mg magnesium, 13.9 mg iron, 6.8 mg zinc, 3.8 mg copper, and more than 1,500 mg potassium. A 5.4 g tablespoon provides about 5.4% of those numbers—around 27 mg magnesium and 0.75 mg iron.

Presence is not the same as absorption. Cocoa's iron is non-heme iron, and bioavailability depends on the rest of the meal and compounds in the food.

Not every unsweetened cocoa is identical

Two products can both list cocoa as the only ingredient yet differ in residual cocoa butter, alkalization, and exact nutrient content. That is why a package label may not perfectly match a generic food-composition entry.

Bottom line

Unsweetened cocoa powder is genuinely rich in fiber and minerals by weight, but the serving is usually small. Use per-100-g numbers to compare products and spoon-level numbers to understand what you actually eat.

faq.question: How much fiber is in a tablespoon of cocoa powder?
faq.answer: Using the USDA value of 37 g/100 g and a 5.4 g tablespoon, it is about 2 g of fiber.

faq.question: Does cocoa powder contain protein?
faq.answer: Yes. The USDA reference contains 19.6 g/100 g, but a tablespoon provides only about 1 g.

faq.question: Which minerals are high in cocoa?
faq.answer: Magnesium is especially concentrated, with substantial iron, copper, zinc, and potassium as well. Serving-size amounts are much smaller than per-100-g values.

faq.question: Is unsweetened cocoa powder fat-free?
faq.answer: No. Pressing removes part of the cocoa butter, not necessarily all of it. Residual fat varies among products.
